post.description: Parts 1 to n with none missing make the object, atomically: the total is held to the bucket's current `file_size_limit`, and the caller's policies on `storage.objects` decide again before and as the row is written. A refusal (403, 413, 415) aborts the upload.

parameters.name: database
parameters.description: The Postgres database (the key's main one when left out).

400.description: `invalid_parts`: a gap, or a part under 5 MiB that isn't the last

403.description: `not_allowed`: the policies no longer allow it

409.description: `conflict`: the name was taken, or the object changed meanwhile

put.description: Part numbers are 1 to 10000; a part is 5 MiB to 100 MiB, but the last may be smaller. Sending a part again replaces it. Its bytes are counted as they arrive and held to the bucket's `file_size_limit` less the other parts'. Part 1's first bytes must be a type the bucket allows.

parameters.name: database
parameters.description: The Postgres database (the key's main one when left out).

413.description: `too_large`: over 100 MiB or the bucket's limit

post.description: Checks the declared `Content-Type` against the bucket's `allowed_mime_types` and the caller's INSERT (or, with `upsert`, its UPDATE) policies on `storage.objects`, then opens a session for 24 hours. Upload parts of 5 MiB to 100 MiB (the last may be smaller), then complete it. The body is empty.
